While unlikely to directly cause harm in this scenario, it can lead to extra follow-up and potential confusion.

Omitting a denial of nausea has little clinical relevance in an evaluation primarily focused on wheeze/shortness of breath and does not meaningfully change triage or management. The impact is mainly documentation completeness.
